ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given $ \angle AOB$ and $ \angle COD$, the ray $ OE$ bisects $ \angle AOD$; the positions of $ \angle AOB$ and $ \angle COD$ are as shown in Figure 2. Given that $ \angle COD = \frac{1}{2}\angle AOB$, find the value of $ \angle COE : \angle DOB$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given information, we have\\
$\because OE$ bisects $\angle AOD$,\\
$\therefore \angle EOD=\frac{1}{2}\left(\angle AOB+\angle BOD\right)$\\
$\because \angle COD=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB$,\\
$\therefore \angle EOC=\angle EOD-\angle COD$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB+\frac{1}{2}\angle BOD-\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOD$\\
$\therefore \angle COE\colon \angle DOB=\boxed{1\colon 2}$

Reasoning: Let the adjacent small angles be ∠AOE = p, ∠EOC = x, ∠COB = q, ∠BOD = y. Because OE bisects ∠AOD, ∠AOE = ∠EOD, that is, p = x + q + y. From the decomposition in the figure, ∠AOB = p + x + q, ∠COD = q + y. The problem statement gives ∠COD = 1/2∠AOB, so q + y = 1/2(p + x + q). Substituting p = x + q + y, we get q + y = 1/2((x + q + y) + x + q) = x + q + y/2. Simplifying gives x = y/2. Therefore ∠COE : ∠DOB = x : y = 1 : 2.
